text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a server-side skip link at the very top of every page, visible by default. It jumps straight to the main content, letting keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks. This costs a tiny bit of screen space but removes the biggest keyboard trap on every page.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s server-side skip link forces every user to download and parse an extra element on every page load—wasting bandwidth and slowing rendering for sighted users who don’t need it. A better fix is a client-side skip link that only renders when keyboard focus reaches the first interactive element, cutting the waste while keeping the benefit. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure page load time and keyboard user success rates with both versions.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a client-side skip link that appears only when keyboard focus reaches the first interactive element. This keeps sighted users from paying the bandwidth cost of an always-visible element while still giving keyboard users the bypass they need. The trade-off is a tiny extra JavaScript payload and a 1-frame delay before the link becomes available—both negligible compared to the accessibility win.

name: Reader
text: Client-side skip links fail when JavaScript is disabled or slow to load—locking out keyboard users who need them most. A hybrid approach: server-side skip link with `display: none` and client-side JS to toggle visibility on focus. Settle it with a live test: measure load-time impact of the hidden server-side link versus the failure rate of the client-only version.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a hybrid approach with a server-side skip link using `display: none` that toggles visibility via client-side JavaScript when it receives keyboard focus. This ensures both accessibility and performance, and the Accessibility Team owns the implementation.
